_comment: Everything the voice path (speech_control, voice_pipeline, wake_word, voice_output, voice_mode) knows about words, thresholds, rates, timeouts and voices (AGENTS.md Rule 0). voice_config.py loads it once per process and checks every value against its documented default in voice_defaults.json (same values as shipped here): a bad or missing value logs one line and falls back to that default, never crashes. Keys starting with _ are notes. DENISSE_VOICE_CONFIG points at another file (tests, a private tweak). Environment variables that already existed (DENISSE_END_SILENCE_S, DENISSE_WAKE_ACK, ...) still win over this file.

stop_request._why: A stop has to act before, and without, the model: on 2026-10-31 a bare 'stop' went to the model and it carried on with the CV clean-up he was stopping. So this stays a fast whole-utterance rule, but the words are data. An utterance is a stop when, after typo fixes, it is only: any lead words, at most one reason, one phrase, any trail words. 'stop the timer', "don't stop talking" and quoted speech inside a question are not.

wake_word._why_name: Her name matches as name_stem plus up to name_extra_letters more letters, anywhere in the transcript: free STT truncates and mangles a bare 'Denisse' ('Den', 'Denn', 'denne', 'Denly'), so it's wide on purpose. Real 'den-' words are excluded below; 'den' itself stays, it's the commonest truncation.
wake_word._why_misheard: Observed Vosk splits of her name into real words. Only trusted when the grammar spotter independently heard her name in the same utterance ('the nice one' is ordinary speech).
wake_word._why_greetings: Stripped just before her name so they don't leak into the command; leading_fillers covers Vosk's hallucinated 'the' at the start of an utterance.
wake_word.wake_ack: Yes Chuen? I can update the config voice line to match the task wording.
wake_word.recent_context_prompt: For background only (not an instruction): the last {seconds}s of speech picked up near the microphone, which may include the current request too: "{recent}"
wake_word.say_study_on: Study mode on. Twenty-five minutes, starting now.

confirm._why: Hands-free mode hears the whole room, so these tools are asked about out loud first and answered by voice. A yes needs a yes word and no no word (her own 'say yes or no' is overheard), in at most answer_max_words words. A word ending in * matches any ending ('confirm*' = confirmed, confirming).
confirm.question: Quick check: should I {action}? Say yes or no.
confirm.no_answer: No answer, so I'll leave it.
confirm._why_describe: How each tool is said in the question. {tool} is the tool name, {file} the file name of its path, any other {field} is that argument with whitespace collapsed, cut to arg_max_chars with '...'. A missing field uses arg_fallbacks.

pipeline._why_endpoint: end_silence_s 0.6, down from 0.9: same WER on the eval set at 0.4-0.9, 0.3 cuts words off; the longest synthetic pause was 0.38 s. docs/voice_latency.md.
pipeline._why_barge_in: Off by default: an energy gate with no echo cancellation, so on open speakers a loud reply can interrupt itself. Fine on headphones.
pipeline._why_abbreviations: Words that end in a full stop without ending the sentence.

output._why_tts: kokoro (local, free) first, Inworld (paid cloud, needs INWORLD_API_KEY) as fallback; 'inworld' swaps the order. inworld-tts-1.5-mini measured ~2x faster to start than inworld-tts-2.

voice_mode._why_voice: pyttsx3 fallback voice: matched against each voice's gender, then as a substring of its name or id (e.g. 'Zira').

stt_vosk._why_model: Folder of the Vosk model, relative to the repo (or absolute). DENISSE_VOSK_MODEL_PATH still wins; DENISSE_WAKE_MODEL_PATH pins hands-free listening to a different one. A bigger model (vosk-model-en-us-0.22) is the fix for words it keeps getting wrong, not more code.
stt_vosk._why_chunk: 2000 frames at 16 kHz = 0.125 s per read: short enough that partials feel live, long enough not to underrun on a background thread.
stt_vosk._why_alternatives: A mangled 'Denisse' is likelier in a secondary guess than in the top one.
stt_vosk._why_gate: Chunks under floor x noise_gate_multiplier become silence before Vosk sees them (it hallucinates 'the' from room noise). 5x, not 2.5x: transient spikes in a quiet room; speech measured 700-1900+ RMS against a floor of ~30-150. DENISSE_VOSK_NOISE_GATE_MULTIPLIER still wins. The floor is the noise_floor_percentile of the last noise_floor_window_s of chunk levels, never below noise_gate_min_floor, recomputed once noise_floor_min_chunks are in.
stt_vosk._why_grammar: The only phrases the dedicated name spotter may choose between (plus Vosk's own '[unk]', added in code). Her name isn't a dictionary word, so the open recognizer sometimes never gets close ('the nice').

stt_whisper._why_device: auto = GPU (float16) when the CUDA libraries load, else CPU (int8); DENISSE_WHISPER_DEVICE still wins. The model name itself is config.json's models.whisper. cuda_probe_s of silence is transcribed at load, because a missing cuBLAS/cuDNN only shows up on first use.
stt_whisper._why_lead_in: Chunks kept from before speech starts (4 x 1024 frames at 16 kHz is about 0.25 s), so the first syllable isn't clipped.

tts_kokoro._why: Local neural voice. model_dir is relative to the repo (or absolute); DENISSE_KOKORO_DIR, DENISSE_KOKORO_VOICE, DENISSE_KOKORO_SPEED and DENISSE_KOKORO_DEVICE still win. voice is any voice in the voices file. warm_up_text is spoken into a throwaway file so the first real reply doesn't pay the GPU warm-up. unavailable_note is printed (with {error}) when synthesis fails and the caller falls back.
